## README.md
# NOAA Coral Reef Watch

Satellite sea surface temperature and coral bleaching heat stress from [NOAA Coral Reef Watch](https://coralreefwatch.noaa.gov/product/5km/index.php), version 3.1, on a global 5 km grid. Daily products cover the last 13 months; monthly and annual composites go back to 1985. Each product is published as an H3 hexagon table (resolution 6) and as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs.

STAC: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coral-reef-watch/stac-collection.json`

## Daily products for the last 13 months (`crw-5km-daily`)

Updated every day at 18:00 UTC. NOAA posts day D on D+1 at around 14:00 UTC. Days older than 13 months are removed; the full daily archive back to 1985 stays available upstream.

| product | variable | units | cell value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sst` | `analysed_sst` | °C | mean of the 5 km pixels |
| `ssta` | `sea_surface_temperature_anomaly` | °C | mean |
| `hs` | `hotspot` | °C | mean |
| `dhw` | `degree_heating_week` | °C-weeks | mean |
| `baa` | `bleaching_alert_area` | level 0–4 | most severe pixel |
| `baa-max-7d` | `bleaching_alert_area` | level 0–4 | most severe pixel |

Bleaching Alert Area levels: 0 No Stress, 1 Bleaching Watch, 2 Bleaching Warning, 3 Bleaching Alert Level 1, 4 Bleaching Alert Level 2.

```
crw-5km-daily/<product>/hex/h0=<cell>/data_0.parquet              # columns: h6, h0, time, <variable>
crw-5km-daily/<product>/hex/h0=<cell>/part-tYYYYMMDD-0.parquet    # current month, one file a day
crw-5km-daily/<product>/cog/<product>-YYYYMMDD.tif
crw-5km-daily/ne-pacific-blob/data_0.parquet
raw/daily/<product>/<upstream file>.nc   (+ .json: source URL, access time, size, SHA-256)
```

Each `h0` cell has one file holding every day of the window in date order. The current month's days sit beside it as one small file a day, and are folded in once the month closes. Read the table with the glob `hex/h0=*/*.parquet` and filter on `time`: because rows are stored in date order, a filter on a few days reads only those parts of each file. There is no `h8` column: the 5 km pixel is coarser than an H3 resolution 8 cell. Join resolution 8 data with `h3_cell_to_parent(h8, 6)`.

### Northeast Pacific warm anomaly summary

`crw-5km-daily/ne-pacific-blob` holds one row per day for the box 20–60°N, 180–110°W: the area with an SST anomaly of at least 2 °C, the area-weighted centre of that area, the area with data, and the strongest anomaly and where it is.

## Monthly composites from 1985 (`crw-5km-monthly`)

Upstream's own monthly composites, from January 1985 to last month. Each month is checked on the 2nd and 5th of the next month at 19:00 UTC, and nothing is removed. `time` is the last day of the month.

| product | variable | units | cell value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sst-min`, `sst-mean`, `sst-max` | `sea_surface_temperature` | °C | min, mean or max of the 5 km pixels, matching the composite |
| `ssta-min`, `ssta-mean`, `ssta-max` | `sea_surface_temperature_anomaly` | °C | min, mean or max |
| `hs-max` | `hotspot` | °C | max |
| `dhw-max` | `degree_heating_week` | °C-weeks | max |
| `baa-max` | `bleaching_alert_area` | level 0–4 | most severe pixel |
| `baa5-max` | `bleaching_alert_area` | level 0–7 | most severe pixel |

`dhw-max`, `baa-max` and `baa5-max` start in April 1985, once twelve weeks of HotSpot have accumulated. `baa5-max` uses upstream's five-level scale: levels 0–4 as above, then 5–7 for Bleaching Alert Levels 3–5.

The min and max products also carry `extreme_date`, the day in the month the extreme was first reached; their COGs have a companion `-date.tif` holding it as a `yyyymmdd` number. Where a cell holds more than one 5 km pixel, `extreme_date` is the latest (max) or earliest (min) of the pixels' dates, so it can come from a different pixel than the value.

```
crw-5km-monthly/<product>/hex/h0=<cell>/data_0.parquet             # columns: h6, h0, time, <variable>[, extreme_date]
crw-5km-monthly/<product>/hex/h0=<cell>/part-tYYYYMM-0.parquet     # current year, one file a month
crw-5km-monthly/<product>/cog/<product>-YYYYMM.tif
crw-5km-monthly/<product>/cog/<product>-YYYYMM-date.tif            # min and max products
raw/monthly/<product>/<upstream file>.nc   (+ .json)
```

Closed years are in one file per `h0` cell in date order, and the current year's months sit beside it until January. Read with `hex/h0=*/*.parquet` and filter on `time`, as for the daily table.

## Annual composites from 1985 (`crw-5km-annual`)

Upstream's own annual composites, the same ten products as the monthly tier, from 1985 to the last full year. Each new year is added on 2 or 5 January, and nothing is removed. `time` is the last day of the year, and `extreme_date` (min and max products) is the day in the year the extreme was first reached.

`dhw-max`, `baa-max` and `baa5-max` have no full-year composite for 1985, so their 1985 row is upstream's composite for 25 March to 31 December 1985.

```
crw-5km-annual/<product>/hex/h0=<cell>/data_0.parquet             # columns: h6, h0, time, <variable>[, extreme_date]
crw-5km-annual/<product>/cog/<product>-YYYY.tif
crw-5km-annual/<product>/cog/<product>-YYYY-date.tif              # min and max products
raw/annual/<product>/<upstream file>.nc   (+ .json)
```

## Caveats

- The SST anomaly is measured against a fixed 1985–1990 plus 1993 daily climatology. It is not a percentile-based marine heatwave definition, and it is less reliable at high latitudes because of persistent cloud.
- HotSpot, Degree Heating Week and Bleaching Alert Area compare temperature with the warmest-month climatology and coral bleaching thresholds. Away from coral reefs they mean the water is warmer than its usual warmest month, not that corals are at risk.
- Upstream marks some pixels at sea-ice edges as out of range. They are treated as missing, so those cells are absent.

## DuckDB

```sql
INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL h3 FROM community; LOAD h3;
SET s3_endpoint = 's3-west.nrp-nautilus.io'; SET s3_url_style = 'path';

-- northeast Pacific warm area through time
SELECT date, area_km2_ssta_ge_2, centroid_lat, centroid_lng, max_ssta
FROM read_parquet('s3://public-coral-reef-watch/crw-5km-daily/ne-pacific-blob/data_0.parquet')
ORDER BY date;

-- the hottest month of each year since 1985 south of Hawaiʻi, and the day it peaked
SELECT year(time) AS yr, arg_max(time, sea_surface_temperature) AS month,
       max(sea_surface_temperature) AS sst, arg_max(extreme_date, sea_surface_temperature) AS peak_day
FROM read_parquet('s3://public-coral-reef-watch/crw-5km-monthly/sst-max/hex/h0=*/*.parquet')
WHERE h0 = h3_cell_to_parent(h3_latlng_to_cell(20.0, -157.0, 6), 0)
  AND h6 = h3_latlng_to_cell(20.0, -157.0, 6)
GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr;

-- Degree Heating Week on one day, near Hawaiʻi
SELECT h6, degree_heating_week
FROM read_parquet('s3://public-coral-reef-watch/crw-5km-daily/dhw/hex/h0=*/*.parquet')
WHERE time = DATE '2026-10-24'
  AND h0 = h3_cell_to_parent(h3_latlng_to_cell(20.8, -156.3, 6), 0);
```

## MapLibre GL JS

There is no PMTiles layer, so there is no `source-layer`. Draw a day's COG as a raster through TiTiler:

```js
const day = '20261024';
const cog = `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-coral-reef-watch/crw-5km-daily/ssta/cog/ssta-${day}.tif`;
map.addSource('ssta', {
  type: 'raster',
  tiles: [`https://titiler.nrp-nautilus.io/cog/tiles/WebMercatorQuad/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?url=${encodeURIComponent(cog)}&rescale=-5,5&colormap_name=rdbu_r`],
  tileSize: 256,
});
map.addLayer({ id: 'ssta', type: 'raster', source: 'ssta' });
```

For the hexagons, query the cells you need and turn them into polygons with `h3_cell_to_boundary_wkt()`, then add the result as a GeoJSON source.
